text:
kelsey: Heads-up — sketching a small extension to the hosting manifest that lets clients express a hosting "preferenc"/affordance (eg. prefer=dedicated, require=private, avoid=hosted) and the control plane/runtime negotiate fallbacks. Want quick feedback before I turn it into an RFC.

kelsey: Motivation: some customers want best-effort routing to Dedicated for latency/cost predictability but still want hosted fallback when capacity is constrained. Right now we either hard-pin or do opaque fallback via routing policies. I want a lightweight, observable hint that is still safe.

kelsey: Rough idea snippet (manifest-level and request hint):
```yaml
# model-serving.manifest.yaml
hosting_affordances:
  - name: prefer_dedicated
    semantics: best_effort
  - name: require_private
    semantics: hard
```

# request header suggestion
Prefer-Hosting: dedicated;strict=false

deepak: +1 on the expressivity. main worry: leaking provider-specific features or creating a slippery slope of knobs we can't support across hosted/dedicated/private.

josh: Could be fine if it's purely advisory and enforced by policy layers. I think we need two axes: affinity (prefer/avoid/require) and enforcement (best-effort/strict).

ana: (typo — ana) We also need clear billing semantics: if we honor prefer_dedicated but then fallback to hosted, how do we attribute cost/quotas? We must avoid surprise invoices.

ops-bot: linked RFC: rfc-xxxx (draft) for manifest evolution. auto-note: add telemetry for preference routing: hosting.preference.requested and hosting.preference.resolved

srinivasa: One implementation pattern: keep the runtime totally declarative. Expose an opaque token capability for Dedicated-like features. Eg the control plane returns a negotiated "hosting_token" with allowed affordances. The request contains `Prefer-Hosting` and we map to token scopes. Minimal surface: a single header + token, avoid expanding API.

josh: agree with srinivasa. Also propose a three-state semantics: prefer (metric), require (fail fast with 409 or 424?), avoid (try to route away, never fall back). We should standardize the semantic mapping.

kelsey: on errors: I'd rather explicit failure for `require` (HTTP 424 Failed Dependency or 409) with clear error body: `{"error":"hosting_unavailable","resolution":"fallback_possible=false"}`. For `prefer` return 2xx but set `X-Hosting-Resolved: hosted|dedicated|private` and emit `hosting.preference.hit`/`miss` metrics.

ana: we also need an audit field in request logs saying what was requested vs what was resolved. That makes billing + compliance easier.

deepak: small nit: avoid adding new auth surfaces. If we add `hosting_token`, it must be KMS-backed and short-lived. Otherwise ops will get asked to rotate tokens forever.

kelsey: good call. Token should be issued per-deployment or per-tenant. I'll add an option to avoid tokens and rely only on header hints for initial rollouts.

srinivasa: edge-case: what about model-specific hardware affinities (eg. quant kernels only on certain runtimes)? Might need an escape hatch allowing runtime to advertise `capabilities: [kv_cache_pin, int8_quant]` in the manifest so clients can optionally request them. But that gets us back into leaking implementation. Keep it minimal.

josh: maybe vendor features are behind explicit feature gates in the manifest. If a tenant opts in, they accept the semantics. Otherwise keep to prefer/require/avoid.

kelsey: rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement `Prefer-Hosting` header handling (prefer/require/avoid) as best-effort + telemetry; 2) expose `X-Hosting-Resolved` and metrics; 3) flag to enable `hosting_token` per-customer for stricter guarantees; 4) RFC for manifest affordances if we need capability advertising.

kelsey: action: I'll draft an RFC with examples, error codes, metric names, and a tiny schema change for manifest. Please drop bikeshed or non-blocking concerns in the doc. ping @deepak @ana @josh @srinivasa for review when ready. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: please link followup RFC in #architecture when ready.
